Inverse-frequency species weights, corrected for domain clipping

Source: R/fn_survey.R
survey_weights.Rd

Inverse-frequency species weights, corrected for domain clipping

Usage

survey_weights(
  coords,
  species,
  domain = NULL,
  min_records = 5,
  p = 0.95,
  damp = 1
)

Arguments

coords

two-column matrix/data.frame of record coordinates (x, y) in the domain's planar CRS (metres).

species

vector of species labels, one per record (length nrow(coords)).

domain

the study domain as an sf polygon or a terra SpatVector/SpatExtent; NULL skips the correction (\(\varphi_j \equiv 1\)).

min_records

minimum records a species needs to be included (default 5). Taxa below the floor are dropped entirely — too few collections to carry a reliable range box or effort signal — not merely down-weighted.

p

inner mass kept by the robust bounding box, as a central probability (default 0.95); the box spans the (1-p)/2 and 1-(1-p)/2 quantiles of x and y, trimming outlier records.

damp

power applied to the raw weight \(\varphi_j/n_j\) (default 1; 0.5 softens the down-weighting of common taxa, 0 makes every species equal).

Value

a data.frame with one row per species: species, n (records), phi (\(\varphi_j\)), freq (\(f_j = n_j/\varphi_j\)) and w (the weight), for species clearing min_records. Row order follows sort(unique(species)).
